key_insight: Fixed orthogonalized momentum can fail on nonsmooth convex optimization, but making the momentum adaptive restores convergence and leads to a practical method called MAGD.
engineering_relevance: For matrix-valued optimization problems in deep learning, this work shows when Muon-style updates are unreliable and provides a safer drop-in alternative with provable guarantees.
method: Analyze Muon under locally Lipschitz, nonsmooth objectives using a generalized derivative framework.
Construct a failure case showing fixed-momentum orthogonalization may miss the global optimum even with bounded iterates.
Introduce MAGD, which blends orthogonalized momentum with gradients using progress-based weighting and adaptive momentum.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence analysis, an O(min{m,n} ε^-2) convex rate with a matching lower bound, and experiments on synthetic tasks, image classification, and LLM pretraining.
watch_item: Performance and guarantees depend on boundedness/regularity assumptions and on carefully tuning adaptive momentum and vanishing step sizes.
